In summary, our research is concerned with
materials that may find applications in intermediate-temperature solid oxide fuel cells.
the synthesis and characterization of perovskite materials with the potential to be applied in SOFCs as anode materials.
the development of new materials with high conductivity for use as anode functional layers in IT-SOFCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perovskites studied here are promising for use as cathode material in IT-SOFCs.
the LFN and LSCFN samples are not suitable for application as cathode materials in SOFCs.
LFN and LSCFN materials are promising candidates for application as interconnectors in SOFCs, however, further optimization of the chemical composition is required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LFN and LSCFN samples are promising materials for SOFC cathode application.
LFN perovkites are promising materials for SOFC cathodes.
LFN perovksites are good candidates as anode materials in IT-SOFCs, but their chemical stability with respect to the electrolyte should be improved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LFN perovksites are promising cathode materials for IT-SOFCs with CGO electrolyte.
LSCFN samples with 0.1 ≤  x  ≤ 0.3 and 0.1 ≤  y  ≤  0.4 exhibit the most promising properties for application as an anode material in SOFCs.
LFN perovkite can be a promising cathode material for IT-SOFCs with CGO electrolyte.
